title: Years of one-nighters and arriving home by bus to his mother
summary: He played Washington, Cleveland, Texas and Denver, then took a Greyhound home, where his mother was ill and his stepfather had had a stroke.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So I stayed down there with her about six...seven years, an' we fell out, so I left again. I left an' went on the road to Washington, D.C. I played up there, an' I went down to Cleveland, Ohio. I worked there a couple o' weeks. Then I went back to Texas and worked Ft. Worth, Texas, about a month. Then I left there...went to Houston...back in Houston...hung around down there about two...three months. Then I went back on some one-nighters, and...uh, played the one-nighters. Then I hauled off an' run off to Denver, Colorado. I played up in Denver, Colorado for four weeks, and then I come home to see my mother. I come home. Instead o' me catchin' a airplane, I caught a bus. I was a'ready to come home, an' I got the urge about twelve o'clock at night. Instead o' me goin' to the airport, I got me a cab and went to the Greyhound Bus Station...got on a Greyhound Bus. Took me all day...practically half the night to get here.

Meantime, my mother was here by herself. Her husband had had a stroke, an' he was in the hospital. So I knocked on the door. I'd been tellin' my mother I was comin' home 'cause she was ill. I'd been tellin' her I was comin'...comin'...comin'...comin'...comin'...comin'...but I never did get around to it, so when I showed up, she opened the door, an' she was surprised to see me. So I come on in. We had a coupla cans o' beer an' we had a good time an' we began to talk about my sister.
My sister was livin' where she livin' at now an' called her up. She came over and brought her...her son...one of her sons with her,
